articles.title_orig: China's Mysterious Spaceplane Seen In Orbit And Docked With An Unidentified Satellite In Newly Unclassified US Military Photo
articles.title_zh: China's Mysterious Spaceplane Seen In Orbit And Docked With An Unidentified Satellite In Newly Unclassified US Military Photo
articles.content_orig:
By WILIAM HUNTER, SENIOR SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY REPORTER
Published: 06:32 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 08:42 EDT, 29 October 2026
A US intelligence report has offered the first clear glimpse at China 's top-secret spaceplane orbiting the Earth, revealing potential clues as to its capabilities.
The robotic Shenlong, or 'divine dragon' spacecraft, has previously been seen releasing mysterious objects in Low–Earth Orbit (LEO).
Since its first mission in 2020, the craft has been the subject of intense observation by governments, space agencies and private companies.
However, until now, no one has seen more than a blurry photo of the light reflecting off its panels .
This first high-resolution image was released in the Defense Intelligence Agency's (DIA) latest Challenges to Security in Space report.
Buried in the 130-page document was a previously unseen image of the plane captured by private space tech company Maxar Technologies, now Vantor, in 2024.
The report simply captions the image as a 'PRC [People's Republic of China] Spaceplane', adding that 'spaceplanes can launch into orbit to place objects in space or even test them and return to Earth'.
Oddly, neither the report nor caption mentioned that this was the first image of its kind or that it was previously classified, raising questions as to why this image has now been revealed.
A US intelligence report has offered the first clear glimpse of China's top–secret Shenlong, or 'divine dragon', spaceplane
The image was captured by the intelligence company Vantor in 2024. It shows that the craft's payload doors are open and that it is docked with a secondary satellite
Much like the American space shuttle, the Shenlong spaceplane is launched from Earth aboard a rocket, before entering orbit and landing like a plane.
Its most recent mission began on February 7 this year, after it took off on a Long March 2F rocket from China's Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center.
However, China has remained exceptionally secretive about its experimental spaceplane and has not even released an official photo of the craft.
This means this image is the first time the public has had a good chance to examine Shenlong and learn more about its potential capabilities.
Vantor, in an update on X, said: 'The report documents China’s expanding presence in space, including reusable space systems, and features Vantor’s WorldView Space imagery of a Chinese spaceplane in orbit in 2024.'
The company's annotated version of the photo describes the craft as PRC Test Spacecraft 3 and notes that it is 26ft long (8m).
The image also highlights that the payload bay doors are visible as partly open and that there is a secondary satellite docked on the rear.
This 32ft-wide (10m) satellite is likely to be a 'service module', a type of satellite that connects with spacecraft to provide them with additional power, propulsion or support systems.
Importantly, this photo also reveals what many experts had already anticipated: Shenlong is nearly identical to the US Space Force's own robotic spaceplane.
Originally developed as a Nasa research project before being taken over by the Department of Defense, the US X-37B spaceplane is a remarkably similar reusable craft.
Previously, the best images of the mysterious plane have been blurry reflections from its panel. However, radar tracking has shown the plane releasing several mysterious objects in orbit
Number of orbital missions : Four
Total days in space : Over 800
Payload capacity : Unknown
Known capabilities : Docking with satellites, releasing payloads, and potentially collecting satellites
Since 2010, X-37B has flown seven missions and spent more than 2,000 days in space conducting secret missions.
Officially, X-37B is an 'experimental test program to demonstrate technologies for a reliable, reusable, uncrewed space test platform for the US Air Force', but its specific purposes are unknown.
However, what is now abundantly clear is the remarkable similarity between the older American spaceplane and its new Chinese counterpart.
Professor Jonathan McDowell, a satellite tracking expert from Durham University Space Research Centre, told the Daily Mail: 'The Chinese spaceplane is very similar to the X-37B, with a payload bay in the middle and a jettisonable service module with solar arrays at the back.
'The wings are slightly different, but the overall layout, down to the tilted rear fins, says to me that some important official in China went to the space folks with a picture of the X-37B and said, "build me one of these".'
However, despite these new images, many of the details concerning Shenlong and its functions remain unclear.
As the report notes, China has two named spaceplanes, Shenlong and Tengyun, meaning 'cloud rider', and it isn't necessarily clear which this image shows.
Likewise, the DIA simply noted that China has launched three spaceplane missions, one in 2020, the second in 2022, and a third beginning in 2023.
Experts say that the Shenlong spaceplane is extremely similar in design to the US Space Force's own robotic spaceplane, the X-38B (pictured)
US-based space tracking firm Leo Labs previously spotted 'an unknown object in the vicinity of the Chinese Shenlong reusable spaceplane', suggesting that it may be releasing small satellites in Low Earth Orbit
We do not yet know whether these were all conducted by the same plane or whether China has multiple operational spaceplanes in orbit.
Most importantly, the DIA has not yet publicly speculated on what Shenlong has been doing in LEO over these years.
Previous radar tracking has captured Shenlong releasing nine unidentified payloads around Earth.
It is believed that these are small, simple satellites called CubeSats, but their function remains unclear.
Earlier this year, Professor McDowell also observed that Shenlong appeared to release a satellite into orbit before returning to retrieve it several months later.
The new report also notes that, during its second mission in November 2022, the spaceplane came within 330ft (100m) of a smaller spacecraft, potentially capturing and re-releasing it.
'I suspect the vehicle also has a robot arm for deploying and retrieving satellites, but that is not visible on the photo,' Professor McDowell explained.
However, despite the alarm this incident caused, Professor McDowell believes the spaceplane's function is simply to 'show they [China] can do a robotic mini shuttle'.
Experts suggest that the Shenlong spaceplane is designed to demonstrate China's capability to launch a robotic shuttle and to test technology in orbit. Pictured: An artistic render of the spaceplane
He adds that it would be 'good for testing new equipment in orbit and then returning it to Earth intact for refurbishment and reuse'.
These findings come as the US warns of a rapid growth in capabilities within China's military and civilian space programme.
Besides Shenlong, China has also revealed images of a planned cargo spaceplane called Haolong, set to serve the Tiangong space station.
Haolong is known to weigh around 7,000kg, with a length of 32ft (10m) and a width of 24ft (8m) with its wings unfolded.
The DIA now warns that China's 'rapidly expanding space programme' is second only to the US's own in size and ability.
Since 2016, the number of space launches taking place each year has more than tripled from 22 to 93, and Beijing has started deploying nine times more satellites per year.
Most worryingly, the DIA's report warns that China sees space as a 'strategic priority for military dominance'.
The report says: 'China has developed and will continue to advance weapons for use against satellites in orbit to disrupt, damage, and destroy other nations’ space capabilities.
China has also revealed plans for a commercial cargo spaceplane, dubbed Haolong, set to supply the Tiangong space station

articles.title_orig: Breaking | US bans Chinese labs from testing electronics ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
articles.title_zh: Breaking | US bans Chinese labs from testing electronics ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
articles.content_orig:
The FCC measure targets testing facilities with alleged PLA ties, giving US labs until December 2028 to expand capacity
The United States on Thursday banned all Chinese laboratories from testing electronic devices destined for the US market, just weeks before US President Donald Trump is due to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to bar testing laboratories and certification bodies in China and other economies that lack a “mutual recognition agreement” or reciprocal trade agreement with the US.
“This is consistent with President Trump’s broader effort to restore balance and fairness with respect to America’s dealings with foreign nations,” said FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.

articles.title_orig: DoorDash strikes $17 billion deal for US rival Instacart in mega grocery delivery bet
articles.title_zh: DoorDash strikes $17 billion deal for US rival Instacart in mega grocery delivery bet
articles.content_orig:
DoorDash said Thursday that it will buy Instacart for $17 billion, uniting one of the nation's top grocery delivery services with a major food delivery company.
DoorDash, which will pay $65 per share for Instacart, said the acquisition will benefit communities by enabling more supermarkets to use Instacart's platform to run their websites.
"Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day," Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said in a statement. "Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery."
Consumers will benefit by having more stores to choose from, speedier delivery options and access to savings when they shop locally, DoorDash also said in announcing the acquisition.
"Instacart customers could shop at more than 50,000 additional stores, on top of the nearly 100,000 stores on the Instacart platform today," DoorDash said.
Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada.
DoorDash was founded a year later in San Francisco as a restaurant-delivery business and expanded into grocery delivery in 2020 amid a pandemic-induced surge in demand. The San Francisco-based company later teamed with the supermarket chain Kroger in 2022 and with Costco last month.
The deal will beef up DoorDash's grocery delivery services, making it a more potent competitor to Amazon and Walmart.
DoorDash's most recent earnings report , released on Wednesday, shows its revenue grew 34% from a year ago. Its total number of orders rose 28%, a sign the company is continuing to grow in the highly competitive delivery business. By the end of 2024, DoorDash held nearly 61% of the food delivery market share, topping Uber Eats and Grubhub, which held around 26% and 6%, respectively, according to Consumer Edge .
The acquisition is the latest sign of consolidation in the delivery services industry, which is increasingly dominated by larger players. As competition intensifies, companies like Instacart have struggled to maintain their market share. Instacart now commands 18% of spending on U.S. delivery platforms, down from 26% five years ago, according to Consumer Edge, a market research company.
DoorDash's acquisition of Instacart  also comes as more people migrate from in-person stores toward apps to order their weekly groceries. Nearly 150 million Americans grocery shopped online as of 2025, according to Capital One .
As online shopping becomes more prevalent, some companies are experimenting with personalized pricing, which involves using AI and consumer data to charge shoppers different prices for the same item.
The advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative has slammed the practice as unfair and predatory. In a months-long investigation last year, the group found that identical grocery items on Instacart could differ in price by as much as 23% from one customer to the next.
Federal regulators are now scrutinizing such practices. The Federal Trade Commission on Thursday said it has opened a probe into DoorDash and Instacart, along with seven other companies across retail and transportation, to examine how they set prices.
DoorDash, which has a market value of $73 billion, said the companies will operate as separate entities until the merger is finalized, which is expected in late 2027 or early 2028. After the deal closes, DoorDash said it plans to maintain Instacart's brand, technology and app.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Iran’s hidden web of military agencies is slipping hardware past the US blockade
articles.title_zh: Iran’s hidden web of military agencies is slipping hardware past the US blockade
articles.content_orig:
Iran has used a secret network of more than 5,000 military agencies to import at least $2 billion worth of equipment, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, bypassing Western sanctions and the US naval blockade, a Reuters investigation published on Thursday found.
One agency alone, identified as MOD 346428, imported $2.3 billion in military-related goods between January 2025 and June 2026, according to shipping records examined by Reuters.
The shipments included rocket fuel ingredients, explosives, aircraft parts, industrial machinery and hundreds of heavy-duty trucks that could be adapted for military use, with goods recorded as originating in China, Russia, Germany and other countries.
The findings provide details of how Iran has continued to obtain materials used in missile and drone production during the US-Israeli war, which began in February, despite attacks on its weapons production facilities.
Thousands of agencies linked to defense ministry
Reuters identified more than 5,000 agencies whose names begin with MOD, referring to Iran's Ministry of Defense, and which share the Tehran address of the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.
Although their registration records list February 11, 1979, as their founding date, most were established in 2013, when Iran was facing severe economic sanctions, the investigation found.
Reuters and Israeli-American risk consultancy 240 Analytics traced the agencies through Iranian banking records, corporate filings and shipping documents, including around 19,000 import records.
Some entities were linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and large Iranian foundations known as bonyads.
The agencies use intermediaries and overseas companies to purchase goods with proceeds from oil sales that bypass sanctions, according to the investigation.
In 97% of the shipments reviewed, transactions were recorded as settled "without currency transfer," allowing purchases to be made using funds held outside Iran.
Banking records also showed that 36 agencies held about $1.2 billion in foreign currency deposits at the end of 2024, while the wider network held around $1.8 billion in local currency, Reuters reported.
The news agency said it found no evidence that the numbered agencies identified in the documents had been individually sanctioned by Western governments.
Missile materials and hundreds of trucks imported
The investigation found that Iran continued importing materials that could be used in missiles and drones after the war began on February 28.
In the first six months of 2026, deliveries included detonators, explosives, aircraft engine components and rocket fuel ingredients.
In February, shortly before the war, Iran imported 93 metric tons of Chinese titanium and hundreds of tons of chemicals that could be used in rocket propellants and explosives, according to customs records.
Between January 2025 and June 2026, MOD 346428 also imported 435 Iveco trucks, some of which matched models used as disguised mobile missile launchers, Reuters reported.
The same agency imported thousands of Toyota Hilux and Land Cruiser vehicles, as well as Toyota Tundra trucks, models that Iranian forces have used for military purposes.
The investigation also traced imports of chemicals to the port of Bandar Abbas, where an explosion in April 2025 killed at least 70 people and injured more than 1,200.
Reuters said it could not determine whether chemicals in one of the shipments it identified were responsible for the explosion.
It also could not establish that all imported goods were intended for weapons production, noting that many materials and machines have both civilian and military uses.
Imports continued during war and blockade
The materials entered Iran through several routes, including cargo vessels crossing the Caspian Sea from Russia, trucks traveling from Central Asia and freight aircraft arriving from China, Reuters reported.
Monthly imports by the identified military agency fell by 47% to $54 million in March, shortly after the war began, but recovered to $77 million by May.
The investigation identified five shipments of Russian detonators worth $7.6 million since January 2025, including a $1.9 million delivery in June 2026.
Since the war began, $27 million worth of goods purchased by Iran's military were recorded as originating in the United Arab Emirates, mostly arriving by sea.
The Reuters data also listed hundreds of millions of dollars in trucks, aircraft components and electronics as coming from Germany and other European Union countries.
Reuters cautioned that some customs records identified shipments only through product codes and declared countries of origin, which it could not always independently verify.
Western companies and governments respond
China's Foreign Ministry told Reuters it was unaware of the reported shipments and rejected attempts to link Beijing to the regional conflict.
"We firmly oppose attempts to maliciously link regional hostilities to China or smear China's reputation," the ministry said.
Italian truck manufacturer Iveco said it had safeguards to prevent its vehicles from reaching prohibited users and destinations but could not control products resold by third parties.
Toyota said it did not conduct business in Iran and had no knowledge of the purchases described in the investigation.
The European Union said it was examining information about Iran's efforts to strengthen its missile and drone programs.
A US Treasury spokesperson said Washington had cut off Iran's economic lifelines and would continue enforcing sanctions.
"While the regime may continue its desperate attempts to evade our powerful sanctions, fund its military and weapons programs, and access foreign currency, we are always 10 steps ahead," the spokesperson said.
Iranian government bodies and companies contacted by Reuters, including the country's presidency and its UN delegation in Geneva, did not respond to requests for comment.
The newspaper said a change in Israeli leadership would not necessarily reduce military threats against Iran but could weaken the political and diplomatic networks Netanyahu has built during his years in power.
"Ultimately, Netanyahu's departure is in Iran's interest, not because his successor would necessarily adopt a friendly approach, but because removing one of the main architects of the confrontation with Iran would reduce the accumulated political and diplomatic capacity behind it," Khorasan wrote.
The assessment came after Israel's parliamentary election on Tuesday produced no clear winner, leaving Netanyahu and his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot , seeking support to form a government.
With nearly 86% of votes counted on Wednesday, Israeli broadcasters projected Netanyahu's right-wing bloc would secure 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition bloc and 19 for Arab-led parties.
Neither main bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a majority, leaving the outcome dependent on coalition negotiations.
Netanyahu's experience seen as key factor
Khorasan said Israeli political groups shared many positions on security matters despite their differences and that Eisenkot, a former military chief, was not opposed to confrontation with Iran.
It argued, however, that Netanyahu had built political and diplomatic networks over many years that a successor could find difficult to replace.
"Netanyahu is not merely a prime minister," the newspaper wrote, adding that he had developed extensive political, regional and international connections and considerable experience influencing US decision-making.
The newspaper said Netanyahu knew how to make Iran a central issue in Washington's foreign policy and connect security developments with political opportunities.
"Removing such a figure from the top of power, even if the basic structure of Israeli policy remains unchanged, means losing part of this accumulated capacity," it said.

articles.title_orig: Finland launches criminal investigation into Google’s clearing of forest for datacentre site
articles.title_zh: Finland launches criminal investigation into Google’s clearing of forest for datacentre site
articles.content_orig:
Authorities allege company may have breached Finnish environmental laws by forgoing required impact assessment
‘Pure arrogance’: anger in Finland as Google illegally fells 250,000 trees for datacentre
Finnish ⁠police have launched a criminal investigation into possible breaches ⁠of the country’s environmental ⁠laws ​at the site of a planned Google datacentre in rural northern Finland .
Authorities allege that Tuike Finland, a Google subsidiary, cleared and drained 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest at the planned site in Muhos before environmental impact assessments required by Finnish law had been completed.
Like other Nordic countries, Finland is attractive to tech companies seeking to build datacentres because of its relative geopolitical stability and abundance of land, but also because its cool climate should allow them to cut energy costs.
“Based on preliminary information, there have been ambiguities and ‌shortcomings in the drainage and water management at the construction site of Tuike Finland ​Oy’s datacentre project,” Finnish police said in a statement on Thursday.
“The criminal investigation will examine, among other things, circumstances related to these issues,” they added.
Finnish authorities are considering applications for a total of 145 new datacentres at various stages of planning, including a €13bn (£11bn) artificial intelligence infrastructure project by Google that the US company has called its largest ‌investment in Europe.
Earlier this month Finnish authorities ordered Google to suspend work at two sites – Muhos and Otanmäki, about 100km to the south-east – after the company failed to complete environmental impact assessments before clearcutting the land.
The Supervisory ⁠Agency, which oversees environmental permits and assessments, told Google to halt “preparatory ​measures altering the environment”. Campaigners estimate 250,000 trees have been felled at Muhos and 150,000 at Otanmäki.
Google’s Finland country manager, Antti Järvinen, has apologised for the forest clearings, but argued that the company had acted according to “the best understanding we had of the legislation at the time”.
The Finnish government has encouraged the projects. In September, when Google’s plans were announced, the prime minister, Petteri Orpo, said attracting investment was a “top priority” and the deal would “deliver lasting benefits”.
But the revelations over Google’s alleged misconduct have sparked a national debate over what datacentre deals mean for communities, the environment and energy prices. The issue could impact parliamentary elections due in April.
More than 93,000 people have signed a petition demanding more datacentre regulation and compensation for environmental damage. Experts say datacentres bring a limited number of local jobs, and benefits on a national level are minimal.
“Really, for Finland, there are no benefits,” said Jussi Kangasharju, professor of computer science at University of Helsinki. “They are international companies serving international customers. Datacentres ultimately have little benefit for others except the datacentre operator.”

articles.title_orig: At least 13 people killed in Russian attack on Dnipro train station
articles.title_zh: At least 13 people killed in Russian attack on Dnipro train station
articles.content_orig:
Russian attacks across Ukraine have killed at least 19 people, including 14 at a busy platform in the main train station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, officials said.
State rail company Ukrzaliznytsia said on Thursday that a jet-powered Russian drone hit the platform where a train was preparing to leave for the nearby city of Zaporizhzhia.
Regional Governor, Oleksandr Hanzha, said on Telegram that at least 14 others were injured and six were in critical condition, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy denounced the attack as “horrific”.
“Just how many terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on certain Russian oligarchs and the Russian energy sector, rather than de-escalating?,” Zelenskyy wrote on X.
Reporting from Kyiv, Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine said Ukraine is experiencing a rise in attacks on its transport infrastructure.
“This marks a trend that we’ve seen lately here in Ukraine of Russian strikes targeting not only the country’s infrastructure, including energy installations, but also increasingly some of its transport logistics like railway stations and sometimes even those railways themselves,” MacAlpine said.
“Also, there has been a larger trend of mounting civilian casualties, according to UN human rights monitoring. Both Russia and Ukraine have seen their deadliest year of the war so far. This is all part of an upward trend that we’ve really noted here in Kyiv, with many, many attacks,” she added.
In Chernihiv in northern Ukraine, two teenagers were killed in a Russian attack on Thursday, while three people were killed in a separate strike on an apartment building in the central city of Kremenchuk.
Russia also targeted Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-biggest city, damaging an educational institution, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram.
Russian news agencies, citing the Ministry of Defence, reported that its forces struck a cargo vessel used by the Ukrainian military in the Black Sea.
Meanwhile, Russia downed most of the 613 drones launched towards Moscow overnight, in a major attack on the Russian capital, state news agency TASS reported.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram that air defence forces destroyed 231 of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) on approach to the city, with the remainder neutralised on distant approaches between Wednesday evening and Thursday morning.
The Kremlin condemned the attacks on Moscow as the city hosts more than 22 African leaders at a summit, TASS reported.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was “very strange” for Kyiv to target Moscow during this time.
The Russian Defence Ministry said its air defence intercepted and destroyed 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight across regions.
Debris from downed drones also caused minor damage after falling onto the territory of an unnamed industrial facility in Sterlitamak, the second-largest city in Russia’s Bashkortostan region, Mayor Emil Shaimardanov said on Telegram.
He said the plant was operating as usual and that local air defence forces had shot down all eight Ukrainian drones involved in the attack.
The attack marks the latest in a series of major drone assaults targeting the Moscow region, following a record attack in September during which air defence forces reported shooting down more than 1,600 drones.
Both sides have reported an increase in attacks in recent months, while Moscow and Kyiv also prepare to resume peace talks next month with US mediation.
Meanwhile, a Ukrainian delegation has headed to the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky, where a localised ceasefire is under way to provide humanitarian aid to the remaining residents.
The Kremlin also said it hopes aid will reach Oleshky on Thursday or Friday and that those wanting to leave the town were able to do so, Russia’s Interfax news agency reported.
So far, neither Ukraine nor Russia has reported any violations of the six-day ceasefire, which took effect early Tuesday.

articles.title_orig: The Duskbloods Switch 2 Release Has Been Delayed To 2027
articles.title_zh: The Duskbloods Switch 2 Release Has Been Delayed To 2027
articles.content_orig:
As will come as very little surprise to all those aware of the ever-shrinking time left in the '2026' window, FromSoftware has today announced that its Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods , will not be launching as originally planned this year, but is instead being pushed to 2027 .
The studio didn't give a precise new release date, but confirmed that it is taking extra time "for final adjustments to game rules and balancing".
The full delay statement was shared on the developer's social media accounts earlier today, where it apologised to all those who have been patiently waiting for the release ever since it was first revealed back in the Switch 2 unveiling Direct last year.
Here is FromSoft's message in full:
While development of 'The Duskbloods' is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.
So no, not all that surprising (considering it's almost November already and we haven't heard a peep since the network test), but it's still a shame to learn that we've got to wait a bit longer. Hey, hopefully the extra polish will lead to a better launch.
The game's first network test back in August was pretty disastrous , all things considered, with frequent crashes and many players not being able to experience the damn thing. Things were better in the ensuing tests , and we winded up having a rather good time with it.
We'll be keeping an eye out for a more precise release date as we head into the new year. Hopefully we don't have to wait for long!

articles.title_orig: iOS 27.3 release date: Here’s when to expect new iPhone features
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.3 release date: Here’s when to expect new iPhone features
articles.content_orig:
Apple released iOS 27.2 this week with new features for Messages , Siri AI , and Photos , plus an Apple Music rebrand and more. But work on iOS 27.3 is already well underway, here’s when to expect the next big iPhone update.
If you follow Apple closely, the company’s software release patterns quickly become clear.
For example, iOS 27.2 launched this week right around the same time as Apple’s previous releases in years past.
The only difference is that normally we would have expected iOS 27.1 in the last week of October rather than 27.2. But due to Apple making iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo , all software releases for the iOS 27 cycle will be off by one number—despite following the same timing as ever.
That means iOS 27.3 is up next, and its release should align with historic patterns for x.2 updates.
iOS 27.3 is expected to arrive in beta within the next few days—Monday, November 2 is likely.
As for the public launch, here’s what past years have shown for comparable x.2 updates:
Based on this pattern, iOS 27.3 is expected to release in mid-December .
Apple always tries to ship its last software update of the year with a little buffer before taking a holiday break. That way if any major issues arise, the company can develop a quick fix and push it out before much of the company takes time off.
As for new iPhone features in iOS 27.3, we’ll know a lot more after the beta arrives. So far though, at a minimum we’re expecting the additional Siri AI languages Apple announced this week, plus the return of the all-new Health app .

articles.title_orig: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge rose in September as third-quarter GDP beats expectations
articles.title_zh: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge rose in September as third-quarter GDP beats expectations
articles.content_orig:
iCapital chief investment strategist Sonali Basak joins Making Money to discuss the Federal Reserve holding interest rates steady, two dissenting FOMC votes and the economy continuing to expand at a strong pace.
The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge rose further away from the central bank's target in September as consumers face price pressures.
The Commerce Department on Thursday reported that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index rose 0.5% on a monthly basis in September and was up 3.6% from a year ago. Both figures were in line with the expectations of economists polled by LSEG.
Core PCE, which excludes volatile measurements of food and energy prices, was up 0.3% on a monthly basis and 3.1% year over year. Those figures were both in line with economists' expectations.
FEDERAL RESERVE MAKES INTEREST RATE DECISION AHEAD OF MIDTERMS
Federal Reserve policymakers are focused on the PCE headline figure as they try to bring inflation back to their long-run target of 2%, though they view core data as a better indicator of inflation.
Compared with August's readings, headline PCE ticked up from 3.4% to 3.6%, while core PCE rose from 3% to 3.1%.
Goods prices were up 3.9% year over year, while services prices increased 3.5% from a year ago in September.
The personal savings rate as a percentage of disposable personal income was 3.8%, down from 4% in August. Over the last two years, the savings rate has declined from a peak of 6.2% in April 2025 and from 5.6% in January 2026.
PCE inflation ticked higher in line with expectations in September. (Will Newton/Getty Images)
While inflation moved further away from the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also released the advance estimate for third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), which grew more than expected.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis estimated that third-quarter GDP was 3.4%, above the 3.2% estimate of economists polled by LSEG. The BEA will release two subsequent revisions of the third-quarter GDP data.
WHITE HOUSE ECONOMIC CHIEF REVEALS WHY AMERICANS AREN'T FEELING OPTIMISTIC ABOUT ECONOMY
Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at etoro, said that "today's in-line PCE report offered little in the way of surprise. But the lack of a shock does not mean the lack of a problem: Both headline and core PCE rose to their highest levels since May, underscoring that inflation remains a stubborn issue."
"The bright spot was the third-quarter GDP report, which showed 3.4% annualized growth and came in slightly ahead of expectations. Personal consumption led the way, while federal government consumption reached its highest level in at least five years," Kenwell said. "The report confirms that demand remains resilient, even if it does little to ease the inflation pressure tied to that demand."
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and central bank policymakers left interest rates unchanged at their October meeting. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, said that the "seemingly indefatigable U.S. consumer and a nascent AI investment boom continue to drive the U.S. economy, with growth running well above trend."
"Admittedly there are some headwinds incoming, which should cool activity rates a little towards the end of the year as oil prices spike and financial conditions tighten. However, the economy looks in good shape, which might make investors question again why the Fed did not raise rates yesterday, especially with PCE moving further above the Fed's target to 3.6% in September," McCann said.
He added that while "Chair Warsh was reluctant to provide strong signals at the FOMC meeting yesterday, a bullish tone on growth, dissents in favor of a hike and the message that financial conditions were not tight all point to a return to tightening in December and potentially one more interest rate hike in 2027, in our view."
CONSUMER INFLATION ROSE FASTER THAN EXPECTED IN SEPTEMBER, CPI REPORT SHOWS
The market continues to expect the Fed to hike interest rates by 25 basis points in December, which would bring the federal funds rate to a range of 4% to 4.25% once implemented.
The CME FedWatch tool shows a 79.6% probability the Fed will hike by 25 basis points in December, down slightly from 84.2% yesterday but higher than the 73.3% probability a week ago.
The benchmark S&P 500 Index declined more than 0.4% after the market opened on Thursday morning.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down over 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite slid more than 1.4%.

articles.title_orig: Hong Kong leader apologizes for deadly fire that tested Beijing’s grip on city
articles.title_zh: Hong Kong leader apologizes for deadly fire that tested Beijing’s grip on city
articles.content_orig:
HONG KONG — Hong Kong ’s leader made a rare apology Thursday for a residential fire that killed 168 people last year, announcing that a top housing official would resign after an investigation blamed corruption and regulatory failures for the Chinese territory’s worst human-caused disaster in decades .
The Nov. 26, 2025, fire at Wang Fuk Court , a high-rise housing estate in the suburban district of Tai Po, swiftly engulfed seven of its eight towers, killing 110 women and 58 men ranging in age from 6 months to 98 years old. Thousands of others were displaced from their homes at the complex, which was undergoing major renovations at the time of the blaze.
The tragedy provoked widespread public grief and anger and was widely seen as the first major test for the Hong Kong government since Beijing imposed a sweeping national security law in 2020 in response to pro-democracy protests. Critics say the law, which Hong Kong and Chinese officials say was necessary to restore stability, has been used to stifle dissent in the former British colony.
Calls for accountability and transparency after the fire were quickly met with warnings from Hong Kong and Chinese officials, who said that “external hostile forces” were trying to re-create the chaos of the 2019 protests, which sometimes turned violent.
John Lee , Hong Kong’s top leader, said he was “deeply saddened” by the fire’s impact on the community.
“After self-reflection, I have considered that the government should roll out a large number of measures for reform, and a lot of work has to be carried out,” he said at a news conference.
“In my capacity as chief executive, I apologize to all the victims and members of the public,” said Lee, who bowed in apology with seven other senior Hong Kong officials.
Lee said Housing Secretary Winnie Ho had resigned on Wednesday, making her the first official to lose her job over the fire. Ho “should bear political responsibility” for the disaster, he said, despite no evidence of personal wrongdoing.
Lee also said the government would make changes to Hong Kong’s construction industry and regulatory system based on recommendations from a scathing report by a government-appointed independent committee that was also released Thursday.
The fire was the result of “decades of failure by the bodies in positions of responsibility in the construction, fire safety engineering and building management industries, and the Government,” according to the 1,154-page report , which was submitted to the government last week and was partially redacted upon its public release.
The long-awaited report found that the fire was most likely caused by a lit cigarette that ignited combustible materials nearby. During public hearings earlier this year, the committee heard testimony that construction workers had been smoking on site.
Renovation contractors also used non-fire-retardant scaffolding nets and flammable foam boards to cover windows, which put the “lives of all residents in WF Court at serious risk, apparently with a view to maximizing their financial gains,” the report said.
The report said that Prestige Construction & Engineering Co., the main contractor, and project consultant Will Power Architects Co. had “cut corners in numerous aspects.”
“There is no doubt that they are the main culprits responsible for the occurrence of the inferno and the high fatalities in the tragic incident,” it said.
Both companies, along with seven individuals, were criminally charged in June on 25 counts, including manslaughter, money laundering and tax evasion.
The report also took a broader view of Hong Kong’s building maintenance and renovation sector, citing a “corrupt eco-system” long characterized by practices such as bid-rigging, which it recommended be criminalized.
In addition, the report criticized the government over regulatory lapses and a “slack enforcement attitude” at the housing complex, where residents had repeatedly raised safety concerns.
“The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues, and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum,” the report said.
Lee said Thursday that the Housing Bureau, Buildings Department, Fire Services Department and Labor Department all bore some responsibility for the blaze and that all four agencies would be the subject of a three-month investigation.
John Burns, a professor emeritus of politics and public administration at the University of Hong Kong, said it was “very significant” that Lee had apologized.
“We’ve gone for years with no chief executive talking about political accountability, as though it didn’t exist,” he told NBC News in an interview.
“Today, we have the chief executive talking about this directly and talking about a system of political accountability,” Burns said. “That’s a positive step.”
He added that it was “inevitable” that an official such as Ho would resign, “otherwise the credibility of the government itself would have been even more severely damaged.”
Mithil Aggarwal is a Hong Kong-based reporter/producer for NBC News.

The remarks come as diplomatic efforts to restart negotiations continue to face uncertainty.

The meeting was initially expected to take place in October, after U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Ukraine and Russia.
The visits yielded an agreement in principle to hold trilateral negotiations, but the Kremlin later declined to participate, accusing Kyiv of carrying out airstrikes on election day on Sept. 20.

The planned meeting follows a renewed U.S. effort to revive negotiations. Moscow has repeatedly rejected Western-backed proposals for a full and unconditional ceasefire, which Kyiv has supported, while continuing to demand that Ukraine cede Donbas .

articles.title_orig: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
articles.title_zh: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
articles.content_orig:
The chaos and horror of Spain's second rail tragedy this year has been conveyed vividly by survivors of Wednesday's high-speed crash that has left at least 69 people dead.
But as Spain holds three days of mourning, revelations from leaked audio recordings of the apparent human error in a control room in the minutes before this disaster happened have given way to public disbelief and outrage, in a highly politicised climate, exactly a month before Spaniards go to the polls.
"You don't know what's happening, you don't know what has happened, you just know that you're being thrown around in a matter of seconds," said Iñaki García, 60.
He was on the stationary Iryo train that was rammed from behind by a Renfe train on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, around 140km (87 miles) south of the capital.
"There were people injured, walking around, there were dead people," he said. "In the next carriage along there were a lot of dead people."
Recalling the horrific scenes around him, one young man told the BBC in a quivering voice: "I don't know if that's something I'll ever recover from."
Stories of tragedy have continued to emerge. A pharmacist from Urda was one of the first to reach the scene, bringing with him first aid supplies and medicine.
"One of [the passengers] was saying goodbye to his wife and children. His last words were 'God is good'," Antonio García told Spanish radio.
Similar scenes of grief played out only nine months ago in the southern village of Adamuz, when a collision on the same Madrid-Seville route killed 46 people.
Now, in the town of Urda, just like Adamuz, awful stories are combined with acts of kindness and solidarity.
Locals turned out to help the injured, bringing blankets, food and water to a nearby sports hall that was converted into a makeshift hospital for much of the day.
"We all started to turn out to help and we organised ourselves as best we could," said Rosa María Domínguez, a local woman, who described the scene as "a horror film".
However, the overriding sentiment that these two tragedies have generated is one of confusion and a failure to comprehend how this could have happened.
Not long ago, the speed, efficiency and safety of Spain's high-speed rail system, the largest in Europe, was the envy of its neighbours.
The Adamuz crash triggered a nationwide debate about whether the network was fit for purpose.
This latest incident intensifies pressure on the left-wing government of Pedro Sánchez, in the middle of an election campaign where his Socialist PSOE is behind the conservatives in most opinion polls.
On Wednesday night a demonstration protesting at the government's handling of the rail network saw far-right groups turn out and clash with police.
Although the main parties, other than the far-right Vox, have suspended campaigning, Sánchez has twice visited the scene of the crash and his People's Party rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo came to Urda on Thursday.
Sánchez's transport minister, Óscar Puente, made clear from the start that a computer failure followed by human error was the likely cause of the crash. By late evening, leaked audio recordings of a control-room operator talking to train drivers appeared to back that up.
Puente has long been a hate figure for the right, and with two of the worst rail tragedies in Spanish history taking place on his watch, the criticism is only going to increase.
Spain's biggest train drivers' union Semaf condemned the leak of audio recordings as irresponsible and slanted. The union had already called a strike for Thursday in a bid to ensure that "urgency to travel is never prioritised over safety".
One train driver, Vicente Almenar, told Spanish media: "They always look for the last link in the chain, where it's weakest, but here the entire procedure failed because we don't even know what our colleague was seeing on the screen," he told Spanish media.
Sánchez had not been expecting rail safety to dominate his campaign, but that now looks increasingly likely.
After two accidents and more than 100 deaths on the same high-speed line, Feijóo told reporters in Urda on Thursday: "The Spanish people need answers. They are wondering what is happening to high-speed rail in their country."
And he emphasised that politics was not about talking - it was about acting.

articles.title_orig: Zwift Plus Explained: Zwift Video Routes & Zwift Coach Hands-On
articles.title_zh: Zwift Plus Explained: Zwift Video Routes & Zwift Coach Hands-On
articles.content_orig:
Roughly six months after acquiring Rouvy, Zwift is starting to do things with it. Or at least, starting to emulate it. In this case Zwift is rolling out a two-component premium tier called Zwift Plus, which includes both an adaptive coaching feature, and a new video routes function. Those video routes are like Rouvy, but…umm…not Rouvy.
Instead, they’re completely newly shot routes in ‘iconic cycling locations’, yet with the social aspect of Zwift riding built atop it. Zwift says all of this began before they acquired Rouvy, hence everything not being Rouvy at all. But, we’re getting head of ourselves.
In terms of pricing, the new Zwift Plus is $29.99/€29.99/£26.99 per month (instead of the existing $19/month), and there are annual plans that are $299 (instead of $199/year). Existing Zwift stays, and as we saw this past Monday, continues to get big expansions.This is purely focused on the new Zwift Coach and Zwift Video Routes pieces.
In any case, I’ve been riding it the past few weeks, so let’s dive into things.
Firstly, no, this is not Rouvy merged into Zwift. It’s so much not Rouvy that Zwift literally went out and filmed every one of these routes by themselves, with their own team and their own equipment. One could (and probably should) have a solid debate about the logic in doing that, but nonetheless, they are indeed different videos…even if the places/locations near 100% overlap.
Zwift says their intent is to keep the company/videos/etc. separate. Rouvy keeps being Rouvy, and Zwift keeps being Zwift. By having a more curated selection, Zwift says it “maintains the social density Zwift is known for”. Further, all the routes are lap-able, though at launch there’s no support for meet-ups or organized events. However, it sounds like both are “fast-follows”, meaning they’re expected to launch quickly.
What Zwift is aiming for here is a more curated selection of routes, meeting a certain quality bar (both in terms of resolution, but also avoiding various road furniture, etc…), and then a continual drumbeat of new route drops every month (ideally looking at 5-10 routes per month). Further, the routes here tend to be a bit shorter (all but one can be completed in an hour), though all also support looping back to the start for continual riding. And of course, all of them will ‘feel’ like being in Zwift as Zwift overlays various things to the roads/etc (which Zwift says they started working on before they acquired Rouvy).
In any case, to select a Zwift Video Route you’ll choose ‘Routes’ at the top, and then use the gigantic Toggle to switch to video routes.
Once toggled, here’s what you see:
There are a few more routes if you scroll down; here’s what else there is – 21 routes in total today, covering 385km of roads:
As you can see above, there’s a good variety in this starter pack, covering Europe, the US, and South Africa. They say they wanted to aim for “cycling icons” in terms of routes, and I’d generally agree with that. These routes are the definition of that.
If I hover over a route, I’ll see the elevation profile:
And then if I click it, I’ll see basically the same thing but with a short one-sentence description. I do feel like these descriptions could use a bit more love.
Nonetheless, once you’ve decided on where to route, you’ll simply tap ‘Start Ride’, and you’re brought to the starting area (just ahead of the start banners). For some routes, they have more of a start corral, and others don’t.
At this point, you’ll just pedal like normal. You’ll notice that there’s plenty of augmented reality bits, just like in Rouvy. For example, arches/banners for Sprint/KOM finishes, bits on the road, and even occasional Zwift vans.
You’ll even see rider shadows on the boards too (just like you do in Rouvy):
Here you can see the green painting on the road surface, plus the boards, plus the Zwift truck:
They’ve done a seemingly creative job at occasionally using these augmented reality bits to hide or conceal things like construction, some sketchy car situations, and more. It’s super well done. That orange van you see head, is actually an augmented reality Zwift van. And only at the very last second did I realize it wasn’t real traffic.
Likewise, I didn’t even notice that this van here waiting to cross this bridge was an augmented reality Zwift van, until I was capturing these screenshots from my recorded rides:
Now, there are different quality levels you can choose for the video streaming portion. Which is *different* than the resolution of the Zwift app on your display. In other words, you could choose 1080p video routes, but then have a 4K resolution from Zwift (which would be things like the metrics displayed/etc). I found 1080p on a MacBook totally fine in terms of resolution, but if I were on a bigger screen, I’d choose the higher resolution video streams:
It’ll do some initial buffering at the beginning, but as I found out on one ride where I tried to do 4K streaming, the hopscotch internet connection I had to where my bikes are in a shed-like place, didn’t quite work out. If you go beyond the buffer, you get orange roads:
The Zwift game and other people and all the still work, you just lose the route video until it catches up. Meaning the whole thing doesn’t stop from a riding perspective. You can keep on riding just fine.
In terms of riding with other people, most of that works as expected. There are some minor quirks. For example, steering round others seems a bit wonky at times. Or rather, just the automatic steering around others doesn’t seem as fluid/normal as I’m used to in Zwift. Sometimes there’s hard and random swerves. However, they do a really good job of effectively ‘fencing’ portions of the road when there’s oncoming traffic, so you can’t have your avatar get hit by a car. Both Shane and I seemed to have the same idea here, trying to steer into this car, but you couldn’t. The ‘viable steering area’ was reduced as the car neared (as I was on the left edge of the road until shortly beforehand).
Likewise, when riders go far ahead of you, their avatar properly gets smaller and slowly fades away at normal human vision distances. All of this feels spot-on.
However, one thing that isn’t super ideal is that you’re always plowing through someone’s ass.
The fade effect is perfectly fine, but rather, it’s the issue that they filmed this to be roughly the same level as you would have your head on a bicycle (which makes sense). But that means when you add all these extra riders, you end up just looking at a lot of peoples butts all the time. An effect that’s gonna be even bigger when you have bigger packs. Whereas in normal Zwift, the camera angle is higher, so you’re not in butt-cam mode.
Meanwhile, you can do HUD-free mode (where you get rid of all the metrics), though not in ERG/structured workout mode. But for regular riding you can:
Now, when you reach the end of the route, it’ll simply ‘loop’ back to the start. You’ll basically teleport back for just continual riding over and over again. It would be cool to be able to ‘stack’ routes together, akin to what Peloton does for workouts (where you basically add things to a queue, and it just iterates through them without forcing you back to a menu). Here you can see me being looped back to the beginning of the route (note the time at 50-minutes, but starting me back at beginning of route):
Meanwhile, shifting topics entirely, you’ve got structured workouts. These worked exactly as you’d expect in regular Zwift, but now with Video Routes and your structured workouts overlaid. I did a few structured workouts this way without any issue.
This is where you start to get into some of the obvious differences to Rouvy, in that Rouvy has a gazillion courses, but also caters to specific race routes – such as Ironman routes and more. So this is where there’s still a solid gap there in that Zwift is targeting cycling icons, whereas Rouvy is targeting basically everything, including race/event routes. So if a coa

articles.title_orig: China’s Communist Party expels 33 officials in post-Mao era record purge
articles.title_zh: China’s Communist Party expels 33 officials in post-Mao era record purge
articles.content_orig:
China’s Communist Party confirmed a wave of expulsions of senior officials ​and unexpectedly elevated top general Zhang Shengmin ‌to the elite Politburo this week, during a four-day conclave focused on tightening internal discipline.
The gathering, the party’s “Fifth ​Plenum” since the current leadership cohort was formed ​in 2022, also set the 21st Party ⁠Congress for the second half of 2027 in ​Beijing, effectively opening China’s tightly choreographed, twice-a-decade contest ​for top leadership posts.
The meeting of the party’s Central Committee, the largest of its top decision-making bodies, saw the highest ​rate of absences in the post-Mao era, ​underscoring the scale of President Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption campaign and ‌wider ⁠political shake-up.
In total, 279 full and alternate members of the leadership body attended the gathering this week, compared with the 376 originally named in 2022, ​a summary ​of the ⁠proceedings dispatched by the official Xinhua news agency showed. This means over a ​quarter of the original cohort was ​absent, many ⁠of them due to purges.
The plenum formally confirmed the expulsion of 33 officials from the party, ⁠including ​former Politburo members Ma Xingrui and ​Zhang Youxia, former senior diplomat Liu Jianchao and former industry ​minister Jin Zhuanglong.

Here are the main headlines from and about Germany on Thursday, October 29, 2026:
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul landed in Panama on Wednesday evening for a visit.
After his arrival at Panama City airport, Wadephul handed over humanitarian supplies to his Panamanian counterpart Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez.
The aid shipment is made up of about 20 tons of supplies. Panama was hit by a powerful earthquake this month.
The supplies include water filters, blankets, tarpaulins, cots and kitchen sets worth over €150,000 ($167,000).
More than 5,000 people are still being housed in emergency shelters, weeks after the magnitude-7.7 quake on October 9, which resulted in injuries and damaged hundreds of buildings.
Wadephul also thanked the Central American country for maintaining the Panama Canal "so responsibly and ensuring it is fit for the future, as well as more generally focusing on preserving balance in the region."
Restrictions on other sea routes due to the conflict in the Middle East has meant that the Panama Canal is more important to global trade than ever.
Wadephul is due to hold talks on Thursday with Martinez-Acha Vasquez and President Jose Raul Mulino.
Wadephul will travel to the US state of Georgia for the G20 summit in Atlanta on Friday and Saturday.
Several names are being floated to replace Frank-Walter Steinmeier as Germany's ceremonial head of state — including some that could be the first woman to hold the post.
Read our full report here.
After delivering his speech at Peking University, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier ditched the formalities to play ping-pong with Germany’s most famous table tennis player, Tino Boll.
In the university sports hall, the two faced each other, accompanied by two Chinese participants — a referee and the university president. Right from the start, Steinmeier downplayed his chances, and subsequently lost 1–7.
Boll, who won silver at the Beijing Olympics in 2008, is the most successful German table tennis player of all time.
He won several Olympic medals, as well as titles in World Cups and World Championships during his storied career, which saw him ranked as the number 1 player in the world in 2003, 2011 and 2018.
To this day, Boll remains one of the best-known Germans in China, where ping-pong is unofficially considered the national sport.
Boll is accompanying Steinmeier as a special guest on his state visit.
Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Thursday called on China to reduce economic imbalances between the two countries, as well as between China and Europe.
Steinmeier, who was speaking at the renowned Peking University, also urged China to work with Germany and other European nations to strengthen the international, rules-based order and "to advocate for peace and free global trade."
The German president, who holds a largely ceremonial role, spoke of his respect for China's rapid development in its economy, technology and politics, calling China a "defining world power."
But Steinmeier added, "With greatness and power comes great responsibility."
"We are not concerned about China's rise. We are watching how China rises," he said.
"We do not want to decouple from China; on the contrary, we want to structure trade in such a way that it continues to benefit both sides." This, he said, requires fair and uniform rules.
Steinmeier was referring to the high barriers European companies face when trying to operate in the Chinese market. Since China heavily subsidizes its exports to Europe, the European market comes under pressure too quickly.
This poses "the danger of one-sided vulnerability," Steinmeier said. Europeans cannot want this for their economy, just as "China does not want it for its economy."
He also called on China to exert more influence on Russia to bring the war in Ukraine to an end.
According to Steinmeier, China's interests are also at stake in this war, just as they are in the Middle East. As a major trading power, China also needs free sea lanes, intact supply chains, and a secure energy supply.
"The longer these conflicts persist, the weaker the global economy as a whole becomes — and with it, one of its largest economies: China," the president said.
Steinmeier addressed future issues in which China should take a particular interest: climate change and artificial intelligence. He appealed to his hosts, saying that when it comes to AI, "we should jointly establish international guidelines so that the technology remains under human control," he said.
On the final day of his state visit, Steinmeier will meet with China's leadership and hold talks with, among others, President Xi Jinping.
Steinmeier is making his first visit to China in eight years, as he seeks to boost bilateral ties.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday said North Korea was threatening "freedom throughout Europe" by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in its war against Ukraine .
After a meeting in Seoul with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Merz highlighted that Russia was supplying weapons to North Korea.
The chancellor said this arrangement therefore shows how "Korea's security affects Europe's security. And Europe's security also affects Korea's security."
North Korea has boosted its military ties with Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Pyongyang has provided Moscow with artillery ammunition and missiles. It has also, according to South Korean intelligence services, sent about 15,000 soldiers to fight alongside Russian forces.
In exchange, Russia provides financial backing, military technology and security guarantees to North Korea.
Before Merz's arrival on Thursday, North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the Sea of Japan, according to the South Korean military.
At the start of his visit, Merz said he hoped that Korea would eventually be unified. The peninsula has been split along the 38th parallel since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953.
Merz also agreed with Lee to deepen their two nations' strategic and security ties, which includes joint military exercises and exchange of intelligence.
The chancellor is expected to conclude his trip to South Korea with a visit to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Friday.

articles.title_orig: Israelis await final election results as claim of foreign interference emerges
articles.title_zh: Israelis await final election results as claim of foreign interference emerges
articles.content_orig:
Netanyahu’s claim of interference in election also dismissed by Israeli police and opposition parties
Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections.
“We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
“They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu , the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote... These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
Iran attempted to interfere in the Israeli election this week and will try to disrupt the US midterm elections next week, the Telegraph reports.
“We have been looking into ways to recruit agents in both the American and Israeli regimes’ election processes,” one official said, adding that “powerful cyber groups have also been established to hack their election systems”.
Meanwhile, another official described it as an extension of its war with the US and Israel.
“War does not just mean missiles and guns when we are under their blockade,” he said. “It also means we are prepared to disrupt their elections, their banking, their travel and all their ordinary systems. We are not in favour of any candidate anywhere, but we would like to see a divided America and a divided Israel.”
Ahmad Tibi , one of the leaders of the Joint List party, said Benjamin Netanyahu was on an orchestrated, toxic campaign meant to undermine the election results.
“This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told Reuters.
During and after Tuesday’s election, Netanyahu and his allies warned against rising Arab turnout and his right-wing Likud party issued statements accusing the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel of “stealing the vote.“
It demanded police and the Shin Bet domestic intelligence service investigate incidents of suspected election bribery and intimidation at ballot stations. It said it possessed evidence of such activity but has not presented it to the ‌public.
The Israeli newspaper Haaretz has reported that, with 97% of votes counted, the balance between the political blocs remains unchanged.
Netanyahu’s coalition remains at 53 seats and Eisenkot’s bloc at 48. Parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel hold 19 seats.
Mahmoud Abbas, the president of the Palestinian Authority, expressed hope that the Israeli election would pave the way for renewed peace talks.
“For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.
“We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together.”
As vote counting continues in Israel , here is a roundup of today’s key developments:
Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies have amplified allegations of election fraud against parties representing Palestinian citizens in Israel. He and members of his coalition have referred the parties to Shin Bet, the country’s domestic security service, for investigation. Netanyahu’s Likud party accused the Palestinian parties of “stealing” the election and claimed, without evidence, that they received money from Qatar.
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, rejected the allegations, saying they were “ridiculous and dangerous”. Responding to the claims, he said: “We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome.”
The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog, has come to the defence of Palestinian voters, as he urged political leaders against “tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote”. He said Shin Bet and the country’s central elections committee would investigate allegations of foreign interference “throughly”.
The central elections committee’s acting director general, Dean Livne, said there was “no basis for claims of systematic violations of election integrity”. The Israeli police also dismissed the claims, according to comments reported in Hebrew-language media, with one source quoted as saying: “Election day passed with very few irregular incidents.”
Netanyahu’s chief rival, former military chief and Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, warned political opponents against exploiting allegations of foreign interference to delay the swearing-in of the next Knesset, which is set for 10 November.
The sentiment was shared by Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, who accused Netanyahu of trying to “undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign” targeting Palestinian citizens in Israel.
So far, Netanyahu’s bloc is projected to win 53 seats , compared with 48 for the grouping led by rival Eisenkot . Palestinian parties are projected to win 19 seats , a record high.
The final tally of absentee ballots is not expected to significantly shift the results, with no grouping managing to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections.
“We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
“They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu , the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote... These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
Both Benjamin Netanyahu and his immediate challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, lack the seats in the Knesset to form a majority government. Eisenkot and his allies face a clear choice.
They could forge a pact with the Arab Israeli parties, currently heading for an historic 19 seats, which would allow them to vote Netanyahu out and form a governing coalition. Or they could enter a unity government with Netanyahu, in return for a ministry or two.
Likud officials are cited in today’s Israeli press as saying Eisenkot will ultimately have no option but to throw in his lot with Netanyahu. Other observers say that would be political suicide, especially as the opposition leader vowed in the campaign he would never collaborate with the prime minister.
However, Eisenkot and key members of his bloc have also ruled out cooperation with the Arab party lists. Breaking either pledge would be costly for them.
The prime minister’s attack on the legitimacy of the Palestinian vote is designed to tip the scales, to force Eisenkot into the Netanyahu camp by increasing the political toxicity of any arrangement with Arab parties, the Joint List and Ra’am.
For its part, the Joint List has ruled out participating in an Eisenkot government because of his bloc’s support for the war in Gaza and the occupation of southern Lebanon, but it has offered to support an Eisenkot minority government with tactical voting in the new Knesset, in the shared interest of ousting Netanyahu.
Even such a transactional arrangement is hard to achieve given the state of Israeli Jewish politics. The only Zionist party that advocates cooperation with Palestinians, the Democrats, won just 6.5% of the total vote by the latest count.
The right and centre-right accounted for 66.5%, while ultra-orthodox Jewish parties won 11%.
Against that background, Eisenkot has doubled down on his determination to form a Zionist government. Such rhetoric makes the prospect of cooperation with Arab parties even m
